text:
maria (AE): Fwd from Dana at Orion — they want a EU-only POC for a regulated payments pilot. asks: strict EU residency for inference + logs, full subprocessors list for EU regions, BYOK KMS options, and an estimate for any pricing uplift and lead time. can we outline what’s feasible for a 30-day POC?

priya (Sales-Engineer): quick summary from infra side: hosted API = regional preference only (we can prefer eu regions but hosted tenants may fail over outside EU under extreme capacity constraints). strict EU-only routing requires Dedicated or Private (VPC). Dedicated = reserved GPU pools pinned to region; Private = customer VPC/on‑prem.

josh (Solutions): important callout — we can do a hybrid approach for the POC: host inference in eu-west-1 dedicated capacity and use hosted control plane (or private control plane for full separation). price delta depends on reserved capacity and KMS model (BYOK/HSM). rough ballpark: +15–30% for dedicated reservation vs standard hosted for the same QPS if we reserve capacity; BYOK add-on varies. i'll run a quick cost sketch. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

oliver (Infra Ops): ops constraints:
- tenant pinning to a single region is supported for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we only have routing preference.
- subprocessors we use for EU deployments: primary compute/storage in GCP (europe-west1) and AWS eu-central-1 for failover; we also push logs to a regional logging partner (EU-based) when residency is requested. i will pull the official subprocessors list and dataflow diagram. ETA EOD tomorrow.

sam (Security): i’ll own the security questionnaire response. immediate asks i need answered:
- exact assets that must remain in EU (models, KV cache, logs, metrics?)
- KMS requirements (BYOK, HSM, key residency)
- retention window for logs/metrics
Once we have that i can fill the RA/Sec questionnaire sections. also need approved subprocessors list to attach to DPA.

maria (AE): dana — quick clarifying q from Orion: is the goal strict legal/data residency (no cross-border transfer allowed) or operational (prefer EU but accept failover)?

dana (Orion PO): strict legal residency is required for the pilot. cannot have inference or logs egress outside EU.

priya (Sales-Engineer): ok — with strict legal residency we must do either Dedicated capacity pinned to eu region or Private (VPC) deployment. hosted with preference won’t meet legal requirement.

josh (Solutions): next steps proposal:
1) infra (oliver) provides subprocessors list + regional dataflow diagram (EOD tomorrow)
2) ops & se (priya + oliver) propose a minimal Dedicated configuration for 30-day POC (instance types, reserved slots, expected QPS) + rough cost delta (72 hours)
3) security (sam) completes questionnaire draft once infra answers arrive (48–72h)
4) AE (maria) confirms contract language (DPA + subprocessors clause) with legal after we have subprocessors list

priya (Sales-Engineer): example of routing/pin config we’d use for Dedicated POC (for ops):
```
routing_policy: 
  type: REGION_PIN
  region: eu-west-1
  failover: NONE 
  kms_in_region: true
```
(we’ll convert to actual YAML for the deployment repo)

oliver (Infra Ops): notes on lead time:
- stand up Dedicated pool in eu-west-1: 5–10 business days if we need new capacity; sometimes we have warm spare and can do 2–3 days.
- KMS BYOK: Private/Dedicated supports customer-managed keys; we need key rotation docs and an onboarding checklist from the customer.
- Logging & audit trail: we can route logs to a customer-owned EU logging bucket (GCS/Azure Blob) — customer must provision and share write access.

sam (Security): flags to watch:
- if customer wants HSM-backed keys, lead time increases (procurement + configuration).
- subprocessors must have EU data processing addenda; any non-EU subprocessors must be removed from the data path.

maria (AE): action item list (owners):
- oliver: subprocessors + dataflow diagram + realistic lead-time for eu-west-1 (due EOD tomorrow)
- josh: POC cost sketch + delta scenarios (on-demand hosted vs dedicated reserved vs private) (due 72h)
- priya: sample routing policy + minimal deployment config (due 48h)
- sam: start sec questionnaire draft and mark required customer inputs (due 72h)
I’ll consolidate and send an options memo to Dana and schedule a 30-min call once we have the diagram. :white_check_mark:

dana (Orion PO): thanks — tight timeline. can we get the subprocessors doc first? legal will want that before the call.

oliver (Infra Ops): noted — will prioritize subprocessors doc and diagram.

josh (Solutions): i’ll flag pricing assumptions in the sketch (QPS, token profile, reserve length) so legal procurement can pre-check.

priya (Sales-Engineer): will also put together a short checklist for customer (keys, logging bucket, network allowlist) to speed onboarding.

maria (AE): great — i’ll draft the calendar invite for a follow-up once we have the subprocessors PDF. thanks team. :pray: 

sam (Security): thumbs up. starting questionnaire now.

oliver (Infra Ops): quick FYI — if Orion later moves to Private, we can get down to fully offline control plane for EU-only. that’s a follow-on option post-POC. :eyes:
